answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should charge a small stake for each identity and treat it as a signal, not a fee: the stake is locked and released slowly only while the agent keeps doing useful work, and slashed if it misbehaves. A heartbeat pulse of verifiable task completions, signed receipts from real counterparties, keeps an identity alive, while idle or cloned accounts quietly wither. Like a garden, the system prunes what never grows and rewards roots that keep producing, so one operator running a thousand fake agents pays a thousand stakes and still cannot fake a history of real work.
